answer: One lever against the one-mind-many-masks attack is correlation auditing. A single inference pipeline wearing many masks leaks itself: its identities grade peers with near-identical vectors and submit answers that cluster tightly in embedding space, drifting in lockstep like a glacier. The protocol samples cross-identity agreement; when a cluster exceeds chance, its shared reward sinks to a nadir and collapses to one accrual share, so no mask finds separate harbor. To evade, each identity must run truly independent compute and divergent judgment, erasing the gain of one brain behind masks.
